title: EthnoBotaPhyWR
text:
A dataset of ethnobotanical uses reported for Orchidaceae species, linked to their Open Tree of Life (OTT) taxonomy identifiers.



orchids_ethnobotanical




A data.frame with 419 rows and 3 columns:


taxon_name


Scientific name of the species


taxon


Wikidata QID (Q-identifier) for the species


taxon_id_ott


Open Tree of Life taxonomy identifier





Each row represents a species with documented ethnobotanical uses. The taxon_id_ott field enables integration with phylogenetic analyses via the Open Tree of Life API.



Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org/) and Open Tree of Life (https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/)




library("EthnoBotaPhyWR")

data(orchids_ethnobotanical)

title: Working with Orchids Datasets
text:
EthnoBotaPhyWR includes three curated datasets for Orchidaceae (Orchids): phytochemical compounds, their classifications, and ethnobotanical uses.


Load the package and available datasets:

library(EthnoBotaPhyWR)
library(tidytable)

# Load all three datasets
data(orchids_compounds)
data(orchids_compound_classes)
data(orchids_ethnobotanical)

cat("Loaded:\n")

Loaded:

cat("  orchids_compounds:", nrow(orchids_compounds), "rows\n")

  orchids_compounds: 3055 rows

cat("  orchids_compound_classes:", nrow(orchids_compound_classes), "rows\n")

  orchids_compound_classes: 1574 rows

cat("  orchids_ethnobotanical:", nrow(orchids_ethnobotanical), "rows\n")

  orchids_ethnobotanical: 419 rows





The orchids_compounds dataset links taxa to their reported chemical compounds, with SMILES strings and chemical classifiers.

head(orchids_compounds, 3)

# A tidytable: 3 × 10
  taxon    taxon_name          compound compound_smiles_cano…¹ compound_inchikey
  <chr>    <chr>               <chr>    <chr>                  <chr>            
1 Q3055749 Epidendrum fulgens  Q100145… OC1CC2=CCC3C(CCC4(C)C… SGNBVLSWZMBQTH-S…
2 Q3055749 Epidendrum fulgens  Q100145… OC1CC2=CCC3C(CCC4(C)C… SGNBVLSWZMBQTH-S…
3 Q4987884 Bulbophyllum echin… Q100276… C(C(C(C(C(=O)O)O)O)O)O QXKAIJAYHKCRRA-U…
# ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​compound_smiles_canonical
# ℹ 5 more variables: connectivity_layer <chr>, pathway <chr>,
#   superclass <chr>, class <chr>, glycoside <lgl>





taxon: Wikidata QID for the species
taxon_name: Scientific name
compound: Wikidata QID for the compound
compound_smiles_canonical: Canonical SMILES representation
compound_inchikey: InChIKey identifier
connectivity_layer: InChIKey connectivity skeleton
pathway, superclass, class: NPClassifier taxonomy
glycoside: Logical flag for glycoside compounds




Count compounds per taxon:

orchids_compounds |>
  tidytable::summarize(
    n_compounds = tidytable::n_distinct(compound),
    .by = taxon_name
  ) |>
  tidytable::arrange(-n_compounds) |>
  head(10)

# A tidytable: 10 × 2

   <chr>                        <int>

 2 Dendrobium officinale          138

10 Dendrobium moniliforme          57

glycosides <- orchids_compounds |>
  tidytable::filter(glycoside) |>
  tidytable::distinct(compound, pathway, superclass, class)

cat("Found", nrow(glycosides), "unique glycoside compounds\n")

Found 249 unique glycoside compounds

head(glycosides)

The orchids_ethnobotanical dataset links species with documented ethnobotanical uses to their Open Tree of Life taxonomy identifiers.

head(orchids_ethnobotanical, 3)

# A tidytable: 3 × 3
  taxon_name       taxon     taxon_id_ott
  <chr>            <chr>     <chr>       
1 Acampe carinata  Q15500570 3975442     
2 Acampe papillosa Q24852981 649247      
3 Acampe praemorsa Q4671836  292057      





taxon_name: Scientific name
taxon: Wikidata QID
taxon_id_ott: Open Tree of Life identifier (for phylogenetic integration)




Use taxon_id_ott to build phylogenetic trees:

# Prepare data for tree building
tree_data <- orchids_ethnobotanical |>
  tidytable::mutate(
    compounds_count = 0, # or merge with orchids_compounds
    ethnobotanical_count = 1
  ) |>
  tidytable::distinct(taxon_id_ott, taxon_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Ready to use", nrow(tree_data), "OTT IDs for phylogenetics\n")

Ready to use 419 OTT IDs for phylogenetics

head(tree_data)

# A tidytable: 6 × 5
  taxon_name             taxon taxon_id_ott compounds_count ethnobotanical_count
  <chr>                  <chr> <chr>                  <dbl>                <dbl>
1 Acampe carinata        Q155… 3975442                    0                    1
2 Acampe papillosa       Q248… 649247                     0                    1
3 Acampe praemorsa       Q467… 292057                     0                    1
4 Acampe rigida          Q333… 140605                     0                    1
5 Acampe wightiana       Q109… 292057                     0                    1
6 Acanthephippium bicol… Q160… 6014409                    0                    1






Combine datasets to analyze which species have both compounds and uses:

# Species with compounds
spp_compounds <- orchids_compounds |>
  tidytable::distinct(taxon, taxon_name)

# Species with ethnobotanical uses
spp_ethnobotany <- orchids_ethnobotanical |>
  tidytable::distinct(taxon, taxon_name)

# Find intersection
both <- tidytable::inner_join(
  spp_compounds,
  spp_ethnobotany,
  by = c("taxon", "taxon_name")
)

cat(
  "Species with both compounds AND ethnobotanical uses:",
  nrow(both), "/", nrow(spp_ethnobotany), "\n"
)

Species with both compounds AND ethnobotanical uses: 102 / 419 





Because these datasets are flat data.frame objects, they qualify for r-universe multi-format export:

CSV, XLSX, JSON, NDJSON downloads
Machine-readable metadata
API access for downstream tools

See https://adafede.r-universe.dev/EthnoBotaPhyWR for format options.



All datasets are curated from:

Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org/) — Taxonomic data and relationships
LOTUS (https://lotus.naturalproducts.net/) — Natural products database
NPClassifier (https://npclassifier.gnps2.org/) — Compound classification
Open Tree of Life (https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/) — Phylogenetic IDs




The data-raw/ scripts document how these datasets were prepared:
# View processing script
file.show(system.file("data-raw", "orchids_compounds.R", package = "EthnoBotaPhyWR"))




Main vignette: See help(ethnobotafever_tree) for the complete pipeline
Tree building: help(get_trees_cached)
Plotting: help(plot_trees)
Compound classification: help(get_npclassifier_taxonomy)

title: Working with Orchids Datasets
text:
Combine datasets to analyze which species have both compounds and uses:

# Species with compounds
spp_compounds <- orchids_compounds |>
  tidytable::distinct(taxon, taxon_name)

# Species with ethnobotanical uses
spp_ethnobotany <- orchids_ethnobotanical |>
  tidytable::distinct(taxon, taxon_name)

# Find intersection
both <- tidytable::inner_join(
  spp_compounds,
  spp_ethnobotany,
  by = c("taxon", "taxon_name")
)

cat(
  "Species with both compounds AND ethnobotanical uses:",
  nrow(both), "/", nrow(spp_ethnobotany), "\n"
)

Species with both compounds AND ethnobotanical uses: 102 / 419

title: EthnoBotaPhyWR
text:
EthnoBotaPhyWR stands for ethnobotany, phytochemistry, Wikidata and R (maybe you can also find the bot of robot) It should be pronounced “Ethnobota Fever”.


Here is what you minimally need:

The scientific name of the taxonomic family you are interested in

Additionally, you can provide:

Your own list of chemical compounds found in subtaxa of the family
Your own list of ethnobotanical uses of subtaxa of the family

Or simply use the included orchids datasets for analysis.



EthnoBotaPhyWR provides:

Built-in datasets for Orchidaceae (3,055 compounds + 419 ethnobotanical uses)
Phylogenetic integration via Open Tree of Life
Phytochemical analysis with NPClassifier taxonomy
Data federation from Wikidata, LOTUS, and external sources




As the package is not (yet) available on CRAN, you will need to install with:
install.packages(
  "EthnoBotaPhyWR",
  repos = c(
    "https://adafede.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cran.r-universe.dev",
    "https://bioc.r-universe.dev"
  )
)
Once installed, you are ready to go through our documentation, with the major steps detailed.





library(EthnoBotaPhyWR)

# Phytochemical data with SMILES and classification
data(orchids_compounds)
head(orchids_compounds)

# NPClassifier taxonomy lookup
data(orchids_compound_classes)
head(orchids_compound_classes)

# Ethnobotanical uses linked to phylogenetics
data(orchids_ethnobotanical)
head(orchids_ethnobotanical)



# Get data for any plant family (requires Wikidata)
result <- ethnobotafever_tree(
  taxon_name = "Orchidaceae",
  n_multiple_genera = 1,
  n_ethnobotanical_count_min = 0,
  n_compounds_count_min = 0,
  example_family_names = c("Solanaceae", "Fabaceae"),
  path_molecules = NULL,  # or path to your own
  path_classes = NULL,
  path_ethnobotanical = NULL,
  export_tree_full = "~/orchids_tree_full.pdf",
  export_tree_phyto = "~/orchids_tree_phyto.pdf",
  export_tree_phyto_sub = "~/orchids_tree_phyto_sub.pdf",
  export_table_classified = "~/orchids_classified.tsv",
  export_table_counts = "~/orchids_counts.tsv",
  export_table_counts_sub = "~/orchids_counts_sub.tsv",
  local_cache = "~/.ethnobotaphy_cache",
  log_dir = "~/"
)

text: EthnoBotaPhyWR stands for ethnobotany, phytochemistry, Wikidata and R (maybe you can also find the bot of robot) It should be pronounced “Ethnobota Fever”.

title: Using EthnoBotaPhyWR
text:
1 Introduction
This vignette illustrates how to collect data on the ethnobotanical uses, and the phytochemistry of a given taxonomic family. The data collected originate from Wikidata, the free knowledge base that anyone can edit.
At the moment, this vignette supports adding your own data and combine them with the ones available on Wikidata to see the results. Ideally, you should share these precious data.

1.1 tl;dr
The function you are looking for is ethnobotafever_tree(), whose parameters are described below:

## Taxonomy-related parameters
taxon_name <- "Orchidaceae" # The scientific name of the family you are interested in

example_family_names <- list( # The scientific name(s) of family(ies) you want to compare to
  "Poaceae" = "Poaceae",
  "Fabaceae" = "Fabaceae",
  "Asteraceae" = "Asteraceae",
  "Orchidaceae" = "Orchidaceae",
  "Rosaceae" = "Rosaceae",
  "Solanaceae" = "Solanaceae"
)

## Thresholds
n_multiple_genera <- 10L # The minimal number of genera where a compound was found in to consider the latter relatively widespread
n_ethnobotanical_count_min <- 10L # The minimal number of species within the genus for which an ethnobotanical use has been reported to consider the genus relatively widely used
n_compounds_count_min <- 50L # The minimal number of compounds reported in a taxon to consider the latter relatively widely investigated

## File paths
pkg_root <- normalizePath(file.path("data-raw", ".."), mustWork = TRUE)
cache_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "data")
log_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "data-raw/")
figures_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "man", "figures")
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

path_molecules <- EthnoBotaPhyWR::orchids_compounds
path_classes <- EthnoBotaPhyWR::orchids_compound_classes
path_ethnobotanical <- EthnoBotaPhyWR::orchids_ethnobotanical

export_tree_full <- file.path(figures_dir, "tree_orchids_full.pdf")
export_tree_phyto <- file.path(figures_dir, "tree_orchids_phyto.pdf")
export_tree_phyto_sub <- file.path(figures_dir, "tree_orchids_phyto_sub.pdf")
export_table_classified <- file.path(
  pkg_root,
  "data-raw",
  "orchids_table_unique_connectivity_classified.tsv"
)
export_table_counts <- file.path(pkg_root, "data-raw", "orchids_table_counts.tsv")
export_table_counts_sub <- file.path(
  pkg_root,
  "data-raw",
  "orchids_table_counts_sub.tsv"
)

local_cache <- cache_dir
dir.create(log_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

Change these parameters as required and you are ready for the fever!

results <- ethnobotafever_tree(
  taxon_name = taxon_name,
  n_multiple_genera = n_multiple_genera,
  n_ethnobotanical_count_min = n_ethnobotanical_count_min,
  n_compounds_count_min = n_compounds_count_min,
  example_family_names = example_family_names,
  path_molecules = path_molecules,
  path_classes = path_classes,
  path_ethnobotanical = path_ethnobotanical,
  export_tree_full = export_tree_full,
  export_tree_phyto = export_tree_phyto,
  export_tree_phyto_sub = export_tree_phyto_sub,
  export_table_classified = export_table_classified,
  export_table_counts = export_table_counts,
  export_table_counts_sub = export_table_counts_sub,
  local_cache = local_cache,
  log_dir = log_dir
)

title: EthnoBotaPhyWR
text:
Collects and plots ethnobotanical and phytochemical data for a given taxon. This function performs data retrieval, merging, and logging, and produces summary statistics and outputs for downstream analysis and visualization.



ethnobotafever_tree(
  taxon_name,
  n_multiple_genera,
  n_ethnobotanical_count_min,
  n_compounds_count_min,
  example_family_names,
  path_molecules,
  path_classes,
  path_ethnobotanical,
  export_tree_full,
  export_tree_phyto,
  export_tree_phyto_sub,
  export_table_classified,
  export_table_counts,
  export_table_counts_sub,
  local_cache,
  log_dir
)







taxon_name


Character. Name of the taxon of interest.




n_multiple_genera


Integer. Minimum number of genera for filtering.




n_ethnobotanical_count_min


Integer. Minimum ethnobotanical count for filtering.




n_compounds_count_min


Integer. Minimum compound count for filtering.




example_family_names


Character vector. Example family names for comparison.




path_molecules


Character, data.frame, or NULL. Local molecules file or table.




path_classes


Character, data.frame, or NULL. Local classes file or seed data.




path_ethnobotanical


Character, data.frame, or NULL. Local ethnobotanical file or table.




export_tree_full


Character. Path for the main full-tree PDF figure.




export_tree_phyto


Character. Path for the phytochemical overview PDF figure.




export_tree_phyto_sub


Character. Path for the species-level phytochemical PDF figure.




export_table_classified


Character. Path for the classified compounds export.




export_table_counts


Character. Path for the genus-level summary table export.




export_table_counts_sub


Character or NULL. Path for the filtered species-level counts export.




local_cache


Character. Directory containing .rda tree cache datasets (for example data-raw).




log_dir


Character. Directory for log files.






This function is a pipeline for data collection, merging, and reporting. It logs progress and statistics throughout. All side effects (file writes, logs) are documented inline.



A list containing the rendered plots, exported tables, and the log-file path.
